transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-19 15:30 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Devon Lee (Redwood SE), Marcos Rinaldi (Redwood SE), Martin Cole (Southgate CTO), Priya Shah (Infra Lead), Lisa Gomez (Product), Aaron Tate (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Southgate is evaluating hosting options (hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) for a conversational assistant integrated into their B2B support product. Primary success criteria: latency p95 < 200ms for short responses, throughput to sustain 80-120 QPS peak, and data controls (KMS, VPC, audit logs). They want a 6-week POC with baseline benchmarks and a cost/latency tradeoff analysis.

Topics: Success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, security/compliance, rollout approach, next steps

[00:00] Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super quick intros and then we'll dive into the hosting tradeoffs, pacing is about an hour. Uh, um, Devon and Marcos from our SE team are here to cover benchmarks and infra notes.
[00:32] Martin Cole: Thanks, hi all. We're really trying to lock-in what hosting mode makes sense — cost + latency are both important. We've got a heavy enterprise customer base so data controls matter.
[00:45] Devon Lee: Hi Martin, Priya, Lisa — quick note on how we'll approach this: we'll scope the POC with three lanes — a hosted baseline, a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) config, and a Private VPC deployment. Each lane will have the same workload spec so we can compare apples-to-apples.
[01:12] Priya Shah: When you say "same workload spec" can you confirm what you need from us? QPS, prompt shapes, token counts? We can dump representative logs.
[01:25] Marcos Rinaldi: Yeah, ideally a sample corpus with ~5k typical prompts plus a peak qps spreadsheet. For sizing we'll ask for average tokens per request and 95th percentile tokens. If you have prefix-heavy convs, tell us about KV cache hit expectations.
[01:52] Lisa Gomez: To add product context — most queries are short, 15-40 tokens, but we do occasionally have long context threads ~800 tokens when we pull case history. We care about tail latency for those long ones.
[02:12] Devon Lee: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll run two profiles: 1) short-turn throughput (15-40 tokens) to measure QPS/latency, 2) long-context path (~800 tokens) to measure p95/p99 tail under concurrency.
[02:30] Aaron Tate: Security side: SOC 2 is table stakes. We also need KMS integration for key wrapping, and SAML SSO into our console. Any private deployment will need to support our HSM via AWS CloudHSM or customer-managed keys on prem.
[02:51] Alicia Park: Yep, all supported. For hosted we have a KMS-backed key store, for Dedicated we can configure customer keys, and Private supports customer-managed HSMs. We'll include the security docs.
[03:10] Martin Cole: What about data residency? We need EU-only storage for certain customers.
[03:18] Alicia Park: We can pin region for hosted and Dedicated. Private obviously sits in your VPC so that's under your control. We'll call out data-at-rest and transit encryption details in the deck.
[03:35] Devon Lee: Moving to success criteria — can we confirm what success looks like for you in the POC? Often customers pick a mix: functional accuracy + performance + ops integration.
[03:52] Lisa Gomez: Product wants 95% intent accuracy on our canonical eval set and no major regressions vs current rule-based baseline. Also low latency for agent handoff.
[04:05] Martin Cole: From infra: p95 latency under 200ms for short responses at 100 QPS sustained. Cost under a ballpark $X per 1000 tokens — we'll refine numbers — and clear audit logs + SSO.
[04:22] Priya Shah: And reliability — we want graceful degradation and automatic fallback to a smaller capacity model rather than having traffic fail. Is that a feature?
[04:34] Marcos Rinaldi: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we'll show a canary + fallback config in the POC.
[04:48] Devon Lee: For benchmarking we'll need to define metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per token, cold-start times, and error rates. We'll also capture KV cache hit-rates for the long-context tests.
[05:07] Martin Cole: Ok. Can you run the baseline on our sample dataset and then run dedicated and private to show the delta? We're most curious about cost per unit vs latency improvements.
[05:18] Devon Lee: Yes — baseline hosted run is quick to spin up; Dedicated requires reserved capacity provisioning which we can approximate with our internal pool. Private will need some setup with your infra team; that will take longer. We'll provide estimated provisioning times.
[05:35] Alicia Park: Timeline idea: Week 0 (this week) — collect artifacts (data, qps profiles, compliance checklist). Week 1-2 — run hosted baseline and share initial bench. Week 3 — Dedicated baseline and cost model. Week 4-5 — Private setup and benchmark (if you green-light). Final week 6 — readout and decision. Does that sound reasonable?
[06:01] Martin Cole: That fits our 6-week target. What are the blockers for private? Network, PKI?
[06:10] Priya Shah: For private we need VPC peering or direct connect, firewall rules, and possibly an on-prem deployment plan if we go that route. Also approvals for HSM.
[06:22] Marcos Rinaldi: For Private, our runbook requires VPN or Direct Connect, specific security group rules, and an account-level config. We'll share the checklist.
[06:33] Aaron Tate: About logging and audit: we need immutable audit logs retained 1 year, and ability to export to our SIEM. Does Redwood support that for hosted?
[06:45] Alicia Park: Hosted supports log export to S3 with lifecycle; Dedicated and Private can forward to your SIEM directly. We'll include retention options and egress controls.
[06:58] Lisa Gomez: On the model side, do you support quantized variants? We care about cost reduction for high-volume short queries.
[07:07] Devon Lee: Yes — runtime supports quantized model variants. In Dedicated we can run int8 quantized models with little perf loss; hosted will sometimes use mixed precision depending on availability. We'll include quantization impact in the cost model.
[07:30] Martin Cole: How do we measure token burn and cost? We have many short prompts with a small context but many API calls.
[07:40] Alicia Park: We'll instrument per-token accounting and show per-route cost. For the POC we'll share a cost dashboard mock with actual numbers from the bench.
[07:52] Devon Lee: Quick note on benchmarking methodology: we'll simulate traffic using your qps profile, warm up caches to emulate production, and measure under sustained load and spike tests. We'll also do a cold-start test for VM spin-up times and model load.
[08:09] Priya Shah: For the short-turn p95 target of <200ms, what's realistic on hosted?
[08:17] Devon Lee: On our curated catalog and small context, hosted can hit ~120-180ms p95 in many regions for 75-100 QPS when models are compatible. Dedicated can get you lower tail p95 due to reserved GPU capacity. Private performance depends on infra sizing — we can aim for similar to Dedicated if you provision similar GPUs.
[08:40] Marcos Rinaldi: Note there's tradeoffs: Dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor risk and gives predictable latency; private gives control but adds ops overhead and potentially higher operational cost. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value.
[09:02] Martin Cole: Let's talk numbers — rough order-of-magnitude. If hosted is X per 1M tokens, what's dedicated?
[09:12] Alicia Park: We'll run exact numbers in the TCO spreadsheet, but roughly Dedicated can cut per-token cost by 20-40% at committed usage; Private can be similar or slightly higher depending on your infra discounts and overhead. We'll provide concrete scenarios in the follow-up.
[09:31] Lisa Gomez: Ok, benchmarks — are you able to run an eval that checks our canonical intent set for accuracy differences between model variants?
[09:41] Devon Lee: Yes, we'll run your eval set against the candidate model families and return confusion matrices and accuracy deltas. We'll also capture hallucination metrics on a sampled set.
[09:52] Aaron Tate: Compliance question again — encryption in transit and at rest, and whether logs contain PII. We need redaction or tokenization options.
[10:02] Alicia Park: We offer PII scrubbing pipelines as part of the ingestion flow and can show examples. For hosted we can apply pre-send scrubbing or include masking on logs.
[10:16] Priya Shah: Regarding networking, for private we need to confirm support for AWS PrivateLink or Direct Connect.
[10:24] Marcos Rinaldi: Yes, we support PrivateLink and Direct Connect — details in the private deployment checklist.
[10:33] Martin Cole: Great. I want to make sure the experiment demonstrates production behavior — not just microbenchmarks. Can we run a week-long soak with production sampling?
[10:42] Devon Lee: We can do a soak if you can provide a sampled live feed or a faithful replay. Soak will show cache behavior and long-tail issues. We'll also note rate limit configs for hosted.
[10:53] Lisa Gomez: One more: can you demonstrate canary rollouts and rollback mechanics as part of the POC? We want to validate safe deploy patterns.
[11:02] Marcos Rinaldi: Absolutely. We'll set up a canary route with traffic split and automatic rollback on error rate thresholds.
[11:14] Alicia Park: Ok big recap — artifacts we need from Southgate: sample prompt corpus, QPS profiles (peak and average), security/compliance checklist, and a small eval set for accuracy checks. Redwood will deliver: hosted baseline bench + metrics, Dedicated bench + cost model, Private setup estimate and bench (if approved), TCO spreadsheet, security docs and runbooks.
[11:39] Martin Cole: That covers it. Any risks we should call out now?
[11:47] Devon Lee: Main risks: representative workload mismatch (if samples aren't representative), network latency for private deployments, and approvals/policy slippage on HSM. We'll mitigate with a soak and daily syncs.
[12:02] Priya Shah: Can you also include a checklist for infra team tasks necessary to support Private so we can pre-approve items?
[12:10] Marcos Rinaldi: Yes — we'll send a Private deployment runbook with explicit network/security items.
[12:19] Aaron Tate: One last ask — competitor note: CloudCo AI offers an integrated managed endpoint but has lower transparency on SLOs; we're evaluating that too.
[12:30] Alicia Park: Good to know. We'll emphasize Redwood's observability and per-route cost insights in our materials.
[12:40] Lisa Gomez: Timeline confirmation: we'll aim to provide data by Friday, 2027-03-21. Does Redwood agree to the bench deliverable dates?
[12:49] Devon Lee: Yes — we'll target hosted baseline by 2027-03-24, Dedicated by 2027-03-31, and Private estimate by 2027-04-07 assuming access.
[13:03] Martin Cole: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[13:07] Alicia Park: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark sync and pass the initial docs.
